requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`.

- **SHA-256 over words and structure.**
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` has a Python case. It asserts a 64-character hex digest, and that changing only comments or whitespace leaves the hash equal. It also asserts that joining words (`"two words"` vs `"twowords"`) changes the hash.
  - `hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests` (in `src/outline/tests.rs`) checks the shared encoder against known SHA-256 vectors and shows that grammar kinds are hashed. It is the same encoder for every language, so Python needs no separate vector test. That test is marked for `structural_hash` and not for the Python requirement, but it only supports the encoding the Python tests rely on.
  - `python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing` checks Python's structural encoding: decorators are part of the definition's hash, and blank-line and indentation changes do not matter.
- **Fingerprint scheme.** `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts `python-structural-v1` through `language.fingerprint_scheme()`, `L::default()`, and the scheme retained on the loaded `OutlineContent`.
- **Ordinary comments excluded.** `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile` has a Python case with a leading and a trailing `#` comment. Editing the comments or removing them leaves the hash equal. Changing a non-comment word (`x` to `y`) changes it. The bundled-fingerprints test covers this too.
- **Docstrings participate.** The docstring section of `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` shows that re-spacing the docstring's words leaves the hash equal. It also shows that changing the docstring's words (`"two words"` to `"changed words"`) changes the hash, so docstrings are hashed as source expressions and not dropped.

I found no unaddressed obligation, and no relevant test lacks a `{test}` reference. The assertions would fail for the plausible violations: hashing comments, dropping docstrings, hashing whitespace, merging words, or using a wrong or unchanged scheme.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
